subject: MATH
title: Math 3
description: Third-grade mathematics focused on the four critical areas of the CA framework: multiplication and division within 100, fractions as numbers (especially unit fractions), area, and two-dimensional shapes. Students also round, add and subtract within 1,000, solve two-step word problems, measure time, mass and liquid volume, and represent data with scaled graphs and line plots.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.3.OA.A.1: Interpret products of whole numbers as the total number of objects in equal groups (5 x 7 as 5 groups of 7).
standards.3.OA.A.2: Interpret whole-number quotients as the number in each share or the number of shares (56 ÷ 8).
standards.3.OA.A.3: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems with equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.
standards.3.OA.A.4: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
standards.3.OA.B.5: Apply properties of operations (commutative, associative, distributive) as strategies to multiply and divide.
standards.3.OA.B.6: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
standards.3.OA.C.7: Fluently multiply and divide within 100; know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers by the end of grade 3.
standards.3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations; represent with equations using a letter for the unknown; assess reasonableness with estimation.
standards.3.OA.D.9: Identify arithmetic patterns (including in the addition and multiplication tables) and explain them using properties of operations.
standards.3.NBT.A.1: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.
standards.3.NBT.A.2: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value and properties of operations.
standards.3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90.
standards.3.NF.A.1: Understand a fraction 1/b as one part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a/b as a parts of size 1/b.
standards.3.NF.A.2: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
standards.3.NF.A.3: Explain equivalence of fractions and compare fractions by reasoning about their size (same numerator or same denominator); express whole numbers as fractions.
standards.3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes; solve elapsed-time word problems.
standards.3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses using grams, kilograms, and liters; solve one-step word problems with these units.
standards.3.MD.B.3: Draw scaled picture graphs and scaled bar graphs to represent data with several categories; solve one- and two-step 'how many more/less' problems.
standards.3.MD.B.4: Generate measurement data with rulers marked in halves and fourths of an inch; show the data on a line plot.
standards.3.MD.C.5: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement using unit squares.
standards.3.MD.C.6: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).
standards.3.MD.C.7: Relate area to multiplication and addition; use tiling, side-length multiplication, the distributive property, and decomposition of rectilinear figures.
standards.3.MD.D.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including unknown side lengths and rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas (or vice versa).
standards.3.G.A.1: Understand that shapes in different categories may share attributes; recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as quadrilaterals.
standards.3.G.A.2: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas and express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

units.title: Place Value, Rounding, Add & Subtract within 1000
units.big_idea: Place value lets us round, estimate, and add or subtract large numbers efficiently.

units.title: Meaning of Multiplication and Division
units.big_idea: Multiplication joins equal groups; division splits a total into equal groups or finds the number of groups.

units.title: Multiplication Strategies and Fact Fluency
units.big_idea: Properties of operations let us use facts we know to find facts we don't.

units.title: Area
units.big_idea: Area measures how much flat space a shape covers and connects to multiplication.

units.title: Two-Step Problems and Patterns
units.big_idea: Good problem solvers represent, solve, and check for reasonableness.

units.title: Fractions as Numbers
units.big_idea: Fractions are numbers made of equal-size unit parts and live on the number line.

units.title: Time, Liquid Volume and Mass
units.big_idea: We measure with standard units and use operations to solve measurement problems.

units.title: Data: Scaled Graphs and Line Plots
units.big_idea: Graphs organize data so we can compare and answer questions.

units.title: Geometry and Perimeter
units.big_idea: Shapes are classified by attributes; perimeter is the distance around a shape.

units.title: Year Review and Fluency Celebration
units.big_idea: Connecting the year's big ideas shows what we know and can do.

objectives: Read and write numbers to 1,000 in standard, word and expanded form

days.title: Build numbers
days.work: Build 3-digit numbers rolled on dice with base-ten blocks and record each in standard, expanded and word form.

days.title: Number line placement
days.work: Place 10 three-digit numbers on an open number line from 0 to 1,000 and explain which benchmarks helped.

days.title: Compare and order
days.work: Compare pairs of 3-digit numbers with <, >, = and order a set of 6 numbers from least to greatest.

days.title: Place value game
days.work: Play 'Greatest Number' with digit cards, then write 5 numbers that are 10 more, 10 less, 100 more and 100 less.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 12-item place value quiz (forms, comparing, 10/100 more or less) and correct errors with blocks.

weeks.assessment: 12-item place value quiz; observation of block models

objectives: Round numbers to the nearest 10 and 100 using a number line

days.title: Nearest ten
days.work: Locate 2-digit and 3-digit numbers between two tens on a vertical number line and round 15 numbers to the nearest 10.

days.title: Nearest hundred
days.work: Use a 0–1,000 number line to round 15 numbers to the nearest hundred, marking the halfway point each time.

days.title: Tricky cases
days.work: Round numbers like 450, 995 and 305 and explain in writing why 450 rounds to 500.

days.title: Rounding in the world
days.work: Round prices from a grocery flyer to the nearest 10 cents and nearest dollar and estimate a shopping total.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a 10-problem rounding check and write a rule for rounding in your own words.

weeks.assessment: 10-problem rounding check plus written rounding rule

objectives: Add 3-digit numbers using place value strategies and the standard algorithm

days.title: Open number line addition
days.work: Solve 8 sums such as 367 + 248 by jumping hundreds, tens and ones on an open number line.

days.title: Partial sums
days.work: Add 3-digit numbers by adding hundreds, tens and ones separately, then combining partial sums.

days.title: Standard algorithm
days.work: Model regrouping with base-ten blocks, then record the standard algorithm for 10 problems.

days.title: Estimate and check
days.work: Estimate each sum by rounding, solve, and judge if the answer is reasonable for 8 word problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a mixed addition quiz using any strategy and explain one solution aloud.

weeks.assessment: Addition quiz and oral explanation of one strategy

objectives: Subtract 3-digit numbers with and without decomposing

days.title: Counting up
days.work: Find differences like 603 − 278 by counting up on an open number line.

days.title: Compensation
days.work: Use friendly-number strategies (e.g., 502 − 199 = 503 − 200) for 10 problems.

days.title: Standard algorithm
days.work: Model decomposing a hundred with blocks, then subtract with the algorithm, including across zeros.

days.title: Check with addition
days.work: Solve 8 subtraction problems and check each with the inverse addition; find patterns in an addition table.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a subtraction quiz with word problems and choose the most efficient strategy for each.

objectives: Solve one- and two-step add/subtract word problems
Use a letter for the unknown

days.title: Bar models
days.work: Draw bar models for 6 add/subtract word problems (result, change and start unknown).

days.title: Letters for unknowns
days.work: Write equations with a letter for the unknown (e.g., 425 + n = 700) and solve.

days.title: Two-step problems
days.work: Solve 5 two-step add/subtract problems about a library book drive, estimating first.

days.title: Write your own
days.work: Write and solve two original word problems using data from a family trip mileage chart.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 1 test on rounding and adding/subtracting within 1,000.

days.title: Equal groups
days.work: Make equal groups with counters on plates and write repeated addition and multiplication sentences.

days.title: Groups in pictures
days.work: Find equal groups in photos (egg cartons, window panes) and write a multiplication equation for each.

days.title: Skip counting
days.work: Skip count by 2s, 5s and 10s on a hundreds chart and connect skip counts to products.

days.title: Story problems
days.work: Draw pictures to solve 6 equal-group story problems like '4 bags with 6 apples each.'

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Match 10 pictures to equations and write a multiplication story for 3 × 7.

days.title: Build arrays
days.work: Build arrays with tiles for 10 facts and label rows × columns.

days.title: Turn it around
days.work: Rotate arrays to show 3 × 6 = 6 × 3 and record turnaround facts.

days.title: Arrays around us
days.work: Hunt for arrays at home (muffin tin, egg carton) and write two equations for each.

days.title: Array problems
days.work: Solve array word problems (chairs in rows, garden beds) using grid paper drawings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete an arrays quiz and explain the commutative property using a drawing.

objectives: Understand division as sharing and as grouping

days.title: Fair sharing
days.work: Share 24 counters equally among 3, 4, 6 and 8 cups and write division equations for each.

days.title: How many groups
days.work: Make groups of a given size (e.g., 20 grapes in bags of 5) and record the number of groups.

days.title: Division on a number line
days.work: Show division as repeated subtraction by jumping backward on a number line.

days.title: Story problems
days.work: Solve 6 sharing and grouping word problems and label which kind each is.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a division meaning quiz and write one sharing and one grouping problem.

weeks.topic: Multiplication and division as related operations
objectives: Relate multiplication and division with fact families

days.title: Fact families
days.work: Use triangle cards to write 4 related equations for 8 fact families.

days.title: Unknown factor
days.work: Solve 15 missing-factor equations such as 6 × ? = 42 and ? ÷ 4 = 7.

days.title: Arrays to division
days.work: Use an array to show that 35 ÷ 5 means 5 × ? = 35.

days.title: Fact family puzzles
days.work: Complete multiplication-division puzzle grids and explain how one fact helps solve another.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a quiz of 20 unknown-number equations within 100.

objectives: Solve equal groups, array and measurement word problems

days.title: Tape diagrams
days.work: Draw tape diagrams for 6 multiplication and division word problems.

days.title: Measurement problems
days.work: Solve problems like 'A rope 32 feet long is cut into 4 equal pieces' using drawings.

days.title: Which operation?
days.work: Sort 10 word problems by operation and justify each choice to a parent.

days.title: Problem writing
days.work: Write a multiplication and a division story about a bake sale and solve them.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 2 test on the meaning of multiplication and division.

objectives: Use patterns to multiply by 2, 5, 10, 0 and 1

days.title: Twos and tens
days.work: Find doubles and tens patterns on a hundreds chart and practice 2s and 10s facts.

days.title: Fives
days.work: Use clock faces and nickels to practice 5s facts and notice the 0/5 ending pattern.

days.title: Zero and one
days.work: Explore 0 and 1 rules with counters and write why 8 × 0 = 0 in a sentence.

days.title: Pattern explain
days.work: Explain why 5s products are half of 10s products using arrays.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a timed-free fact check on 2, 5, 10, 0 and 1 and record facts to practice.

weeks.topic: Facts of 3, 4, 6 and the distributive property
objectives: Use doubling and the distributive property to find 3s, 4s, 6s

days.title: Threes
days.work: Use 2s facts plus one more group to solve 3s facts with arrays.

days.title: Fours as doubles
days.work: Double 2s facts to find 4s facts and record in a table.

days.title: Break apart arrays
days.work: Split arrays such as 6 × 7 into 5 × 7 + 1 × 7 and color each part.

days.title: Sixes
days.work: Use 5s plus one group and 3s doubled to learn 6s facts; play a fact war card game.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve a mixed 3s/4s/6s quiz and explain one fact using the distributive property.

weeks.assessment: Mixed facts quiz with distributive explanation

weeks.topic: Facts of 7, 8, 9 and the associative property
objectives: Use known facts and the associative property to solve 7s, 8s, 9s
Find patterns in the multiplication table

days.title: Nines patterns
days.work: Find the tens-ones pattern in 9s and practice with the finger trick and 10s minus a group.

days.title: Eights
days.work: Double 4s facts to find 8s; solve 2 × 4 × 3 two ways to show the associative property.

days.title: Sevens
days.work: Use 5s + 2s to find 7s facts and practice with a fact board game.

days.title: Table patterns
days.work: Shade patterns in a multiplication table (diagonal squares, even products) and explain them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 40-fact mixed check and set a fluency goal.

weeks.topic: Multiplying by multiples of 10 and fluency
objectives: Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10

days.title: Tens rods
days.work: Model 4 × 30 with tens rods and record as 4 × 3 tens = 12 tens = 120.

days.title: Pattern practice
days.work: Solve sets like 6 × 7, 6 × 70 and explain the place-value pattern.

days.title: Word problems
days.work: Solve 6 problems such as '8 boxes of 40 crayons' and check with skip counting by tens.

days.title: Division fluency
days.work: Practice division facts with fact family cards and a Math Playground fact game.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 3 test on strategies, properties and multiples of 10, plus a fluency check.

objectives: Define area as covering a flat surface

days.title: Cover it
days.work: Cover book covers and placemats with sticky notes and count to find area in improvised units.

days.title: Square units
days.work: Measure shapes on grid paper by counting square centimeters and square inches.

days.title: Compare areas
days.work: Build three different shapes with 12 tiles each and explain why they have the same area.

days.title: Square feet
days.work: Make a square-foot paper template and estimate then measure the area of a rug.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Find the areas of 10 shapes on grid paper and explain why units must not overlap.

weeks.assessment: Area by counting square units check

objectives: Relate tiling to multiplying side lengths
Find area of rectangles with formulas and arrays

days.title: Tile and count
days.work: Tile rectangles and show that rows × columns gives the same total as counting.

days.title: Multiply sides
days.work: Measure side lengths of rectangles drawn on grid paper and multiply to find area.

days.title: Unknown side
days.work: Solve problems like 'A rug has area 24 sq ft and width 4 ft; how long is it?'

days.title: Distributive area
days.work: Split a 7 × 8 rectangle into 7 × 5 and 7 × 3 and add the areas.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete 8 area problems using multiplication and the distributive property.

objectives: Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing

days.title: Decompose shapes
days.work: Split L-shaped figures into rectangles and add their areas.

days.title: Two ways
days.work: Find the area of the same figure two different ways and compare.

days.title: Room design
days.work: Design a dream bedroom floor plan on grid paper and calculate each area.

days.title: Garden problems
days.work: Solve area word problems about garden plots and patios.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 4 test on area concepts and composite figures.

weeks.topic: Two-step word problems with four operations
objectives: Solve two-step problems with all four operations

days.title: Plan the steps
days.work: Underline the question and plan both steps for 5 two-step problems before solving.

days.title: Equations with letters
days.work: Write a single equation with a letter for the unknown for each two-step problem.

days.title: Estimate first
days.work: Estimate answers with rounding and mental math before solving; check reasonableness.

days.title: Party planning
days.work: Solve a multi-step party budget problem (packs of plates, cost, change).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a two-step problem quiz and explain one solution with a bar model.

objectives: Identify and explain patterns in tables

days.title: Even and odd
days.work: Investigate whether sums and products of evens and odds are even or odd.

days.title: Table patterns
days.work: Find and color patterns in the addition table and write rules.

days.title: Input/output
days.work: Complete input-output tables and name the rule.

days.title: Explain it
days.work: Write an explanation of why 4 times any number is always even.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Complete a short test on two-step problems and patterns plus a mixed fact check.

days.title: Equal parts
days.work: Fold paper rectangles and circles into halves, thirds, fourths, sixths and eighths.

days.title: Unit fractions
days.work: Label each part as a unit fraction and explain why parts must be equal.

days.title: Same area, different shape
days.work: Partition squares into fourths in 3 different ways and prove each part has equal area.

days.title: Fraction strips
days.work: Make a set of fraction strips (1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8) to use throughout the unit.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Identify and draw unit fractions for 10 shapes.

objectives: Understand a/b as a parts of size 1/b

days.title: Building fractions
days.work: Build 3/4, 5/6 and 2/3 by joining unit fraction strips.

days.title: Pattern blocks
days.work: Use pattern blocks with the hexagon as one whole to show halves, thirds and sixths.

days.title: Fractions of a set
days.work: Explore fractions of a group of 8 counters, e.g., 3/8 are red.

days.title: Pizza problems
days.work: Solve fraction stories like 'Ana ate 3 of 8 equal slices; what fraction did she eat?'

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write fractions for 12 shaded models and draw models for 4 fractions.

objectives: Place fractions on a number line

days.title: Partition 0 to 1
days.work: Divide number lines from 0 to 1 into equal intervals and label unit fractions.

days.title: Locate a/b
days.work: Mark 3/4, 5/8 and 2/3 on number lines by counting unit lengths.

days.title: Beyond one
days.work: Extend number lines to 2 and label fractions like 5/4 and 6/3.

days.title: Ruler fractions
days.work: Find halves and fourths of an inch on a ruler and connect to the number line.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Place 10 fractions on number lines and explain how you located each.

objectives: Recognize and generate equivalent fractions with models

days.title: Strip equivalents
days.work: Use fraction strips to find fractions equal to 1/2, 1/3 and 3/4.

days.title: Number line equivalents
days.work: Stack number lines for halves, fourths and eighths and mark equivalent points.

days.title: Whole numbers
days.work: Show that 3 = 3/1 and 1 = 4/4 = 6/6 with models.

days.title: Equivalence game
days.work: Play a matching game with equivalent fraction cards and explain matches.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete an equivalent fractions quiz with models.

objectives: Compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator

days.title: Same denominator
days.work: Compare fractions like 3/8 and 5/8 with strips and record with <, >, =.

days.title: Same numerator
days.work: Compare 2/3 and 2/6 and explain why more pieces means smaller pieces.

days.title: Same whole
days.work: Explain why comparisons only work when the wholes are the same size, using two different pizzas.

days.title: Fraction war
days.work: Play fraction war with cards, justifying each comparison with a drawing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare 12 pairs of fractions and justify 3 in writing.

days.title: Recipe fractions
days.work: Read a simple recipe and model 1/2, 3/4 and 1/3 cup amounts with measuring cups.

days.title: Garden plot
days.work: Partition a garden drawing into equal areas and write each as a unit fraction.

days.title: Fraction stations
days.work: Rotate through number line, comparison and equivalence stations.

days.title: Error analysis
days.work: Find and fix errors in 5 worked fraction problems.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 6 test on fractions.

weeks.topic: Time to the minute and elapsed time
objectives: Tell time to the nearest minute

days.title: Nearest minute
days.work: Read and set an analog clock to the nearest minute for 15 times.

days.title: Elapsed on a number line
days.work: Use an open number line to find elapsed time between start and end times.

days.title: Start and end unknown
days.work: Solve problems where the start time or end time is unknown.

days.title: Daily schedule
days.work: Record your day's schedule and calculate the length of 5 activities.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a time and elapsed-time quiz.

objectives: Estimate and measure liquid volume in liters and milliliters

days.title: Liter benchmark
days.work: Fill a 1-liter bottle and estimate which household containers hold more or less than 1 liter.

days.title: Measure containers
days.work: Measure the capacity of 5 containers with a marked liter bottle and record in a table.

days.title: Read scales
days.work: Read liquid levels on beaker diagrams with different scales.

days.title: Volume problems
days.work: Solve add/subtract/multiply word problems with liters (e.g., 4 jugs of 3 L).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a liquid volume quiz and estimation challenge.

objectives: Estimate and measure mass in grams and kilograms

days.title: Gram and kilogram
days.work: Hold a paper clip (about 1 g) and a 1 kg bag of rice as benchmarks; estimate 8 objects.

days.title: Weigh objects
days.work: Use a kitchen scale to measure the mass of 8 objects and compare to estimates.

days.title: Balance scale
days.work: Build a hanger balance and compare masses of two objects.

days.title: Mass problems
days.work: Solve one-step word problems about mass of fruit and packages.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 7 test on time, liquid volume and mass.

weeks.topic: Scaled picture graphs and bar graphs
objectives: Create scaled picture and bar graphs

days.title: Read scaled graphs
days.work: Read picture graphs where one symbol equals 5 and answer questions.

days.title: Survey
days.work: Survey family and friends about favorite fruits and tally the results.

days.title: Make a bar graph
days.work: Draw a scaled bar graph (scale of 2) of the survey data.

days.title: Compare data
days.work: Answer one- and two-step 'how many more/fewer' questions from your graph.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Interpret a new scaled graph and create a picture graph with a key.

objectives: Measure to the nearest half and quarter inch

days.title: Ruler fractions
days.work: Practice measuring lines to the nearest half and quarter inch.

days.title: Collect data
days.work: Measure 15 leaves or pencils to the nearest quarter inch and record.

days.title: Line plot
days.work: Create a line plot with the data, labeling the scale in fourths.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Answer questions about the line plot: most common length, longest, shortest.

days.title: Unit 8 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 8 test on graphs and line plots.

days.title: Sort shapes
days.work: Sort shape cards by sides, angles and parallel sides and name each sort.

days.title: Quadrilateral family
days.work: Make a chart showing how squares, rectangles and rhombuses are all quadrilaterals.

days.title: Geoboard builds
days.work: Build quadrilaterals on a geoboard or dot paper that are not rectangles, rhombuses or squares.

days.title: Always, sometimes, never
days.work: Discuss statements like 'A square is a rhombus' and justify.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a shape attributes quiz.

days.title: Measure around
days.work: Use string and a ruler to find the perimeter of books, a table and a picture frame.

days.title: Polygons
days.work: Find perimeters of polygons on grid paper by adding side lengths.

days.title: Unknown side
days.work: Find a missing side length when the perimeter is known.

days.title: Fence problems
days.work: Solve fencing word problems for a dog pen and garden.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a perimeter quiz.

objectives: Compare rectangles with same perimeter and different area
Compare same area and different perimeter

days.title: Same area
days.work: Build all rectangles with area 24 and record their perimeters.

days.title: Same perimeter
days.work: Draw all rectangles with perimeter 20 and record their areas.

days.title: Best pen
days.work: Find the rectangular pen with the most area using 24 feet of fence.

days.title: Area or perimeter?
days.work: Decide whether 10 real-life situations need area or perimeter.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve a mixed area/perimeter problem set.

objectives: Apply geometry, area and perimeter in a design

days.title: Park design
days.work: Begin designing a neighborhood park on grid paper with at least 4 rectangular areas.

days.title: Measure the park
days.work: Calculate area and perimeter for each section of the park.

days.title: Fair share
days.work: Partition the picnic area into equal parts for 4 families and name each fraction.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the park design and explain calculations to the family.

days.title: Unit 9 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 9 test on geometry, area and perimeter.

weeks.assessment: Unit 9 test and park design project

objectives: Demonstrate fluency with multiplication/division within 100 and add/subtract within 1,000

days.title: Fact fluency
days.work: Complete a full multiplication and division fact assessment.

days.title: Add/subtract review
days.work: Solve mixed 3-digit add/subtract problems with estimation.

days.title: Problem solving
days.work: Solve 5 multi-step word problems and explain thinking.

days.title: Math games day
days.work: Play a fact board game and a target-number game to practice operations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a cumulative operations test.

days.title: Fraction review
days.work: Review equivalence and comparison with strips and number lines.

days.title: Measurement review
days.work: Review time, volume, mass and area problems.

days.title: Geometry review
days.work: Review quadrilaterals and perimeter with a scavenger hunt.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Complete the end-of-year math assessment.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Build a math portfolio of best work and write a reflection on growth.
